Weight Robustness Diagnostic for the Decision Band

Source: R/weight_robustness.R
sci_weight_robustness.Rd

Auto-perturbs the pillar weights around the current configuration and reports the smallest weight change that flips the reported decision band. It answers a single question: is our band robust to the weights we chose?

Usage

sci_weight_robustness(
  evidence,
  config = sci_config_default(),
  step = 0.005,
  max_shift = 0.5,
  methods = c("oat", "transfer"),
  n_critical = NULL
)

Arguments

evidence

A validated evidence data.frame.

config

An sci_config from sci_config_default(). Its pillar_weights define the point the scan perturbs around.

step

Positive numeric grid resolution for the shift search (default 0.005).

max_shift

Largest shift magnitude to explore, in weight units (default 0.5).

methods

Character vector choosing the perturbation families to run: any of "oat" and "transfer" (both by default).

n_critical

Number of open critical findings. When NULL (the default) it is taken from the evidence through compute_pillar_scores(), exactly as in a standard run. It is held fixed across all perturbations.

Value

A list of class "sci_weight_robustness" with:

  • baseline_sci: the unperturbed SCI (numeric 0–100)

  • baseline_band: the unperturbed decision band

  • weights: named numeric vector of the weights scanned around

  • min_shift: smallest weight change (any move) that flips the band, or NA when no flip was found within max_shift

  • robust: TRUE when no flip was found within max_shift

  • moves: a tidy tibble, one row per move tested, with columns method, move, pillar, to, direction, min_shift, new_band, and flips

  • max_shift, step: the search settings used

Details

This is a robustness diagnostic, not a calibration or validation of the weights. It does not say which weights are correct, nor does it propose new ones. It only measures how far the current weights can move before the decision band would change, so you know whether the band is sitting safely inside its weight neighbourhood or balanced on a knife edge.

The scan reuses the existing compute_sci() and classify_band() exactly. Pillar scores depend only on the evidence (not on the weights), so they are computed once from config and held fixed; only the pillar weights are perturbed. The number of open critical findings is held fixed too, so the non-compensatory gate behaves exactly as in the unperturbed run.

Two families of perturbation are explored:

  • One-at-a-time ("oat"): each pillar's weight is nudged up and down by a growing shift, with the remaining weights rescaled proportionally so the vector still sums to 1. The reported magnitude is the absolute change in the nudged pillar's weight.

  • Transfer ("transfer"): a small mass is moved along the simplex from one pillar to another (a directed pairwise step). The reported magnitude is the mass moved.

For every move the scan grows the shift from step up to max_shift and records the first magnitude at which the band flips, if any.

See also

sci_sensitivity_analysis() for scoring explicit weight scenarios.

Examples

ctx <- r4subcore::r4sub_run_context(study_id = "DEMO", environment = "DEV")
#> ℹ Run context created: "R4S-20261115072749-6glbznel"
ev <- r4subcore::as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "dataset", asset_id = "ADSL", source_name = "demo",
    source_version = NA_character_,
    indicator_id = c("Q1", "T1", "R1", "U1"),
    indicator_name = c("q", "t", "r", "u"),
    indicator_domain = c("quality", "trace", "risk", "usability"),
    severity = c("high", "low", "medium", "low"),
    result = c("warn", "pass", "pass", "pass"),
    metric_value = NA_real_, metric_unit = NA_character_,
    message = NA_character_, location = NA_character_,
    evidence_payload = "{}", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
)
#> ✔ Evidence table created: 4 rows

rob <- sci_weight_robustness(ev)
rob
#> 
#> ── SCI weight robustness (diagnostic) 
#> ℹ Baseline SCI 46.9, band "high_risk".
#> ! Smallest weight change that flips the band: 0.035.
#> ℹ   quality -> trace (shift 0.035) -> unclassified
#> ℹ   quality -> usability (shift 0.035) -> unclassified
#> ℹ   decrease quality (shift 0.045) -> unclassified
#> Diagnostic only: this probes band stability, not whether the weights are
#> correct.
rob$min_shift
#> [1] 0.035
